newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed amid sagging volumes.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed amid sagging volumes.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed after a flat, sluggishly traded session, floor sources said.
Firmness came from news India had stopped wheat exports and on spillover from a technical bounce in CBOT soybeans and, to a lesser extent, corn, traders said.
Weakness showed up in the form of forecasts for more clear, dry weather this week in the central Plains, which should allow planting to progress rapidly.
Traders said the Dec/March spread traded out to 16 cents per bushel from around 15 cents Friday.
KCBT wheat settled two cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with Dec up 3/4 cents at $4.35-1/4. March lost 1/4 cent to close at $4.20-3/4.
Traders said CIS sold 1.3 million Dec bushels and LFG sold 1.5 million Dec and 500,000 March. Wolcott & Lincoln bull-spread 700,000 Dec/March at 16 cents.
The KCBT estimated Monday's wheat futures volume at 17.97 million bushels, a sharp decrease from Friday's volume of 30.835 million.
